name: Audience Adaptation Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building audience adaptation — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary audience adaptation tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building audience adaptation — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary audience adaptation tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep audience adaptation changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
2. When audience adaptation decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. Before starting audience adaptation work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to audience adaptation (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen audience adaptation approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Validate audience adaptation outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. Prefer explicit, readable audience adaptation solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
8. State assumptions about audience adaptation explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic audience adaptation advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new audience adaptation abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of audience adaptation correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for audience adaptation, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
